synthesis.description: ISO and FERC notices on market rules, price caps, settlement figures, operating procedures, outages and calls arrive from CAISO communications and regulatory staff. Bill Williams and others forward the relevant ones to traders and analysts with commentary, ask colleagues what an order means for the desk, set up meetings to discuss pros and cons, request test access for system changes, and review draft documents for comment by stated deadlines.
steps: An ISO, FERC or market notice arrives from CAISO or regulatory staff.
A desk lead reads it and judges whether it affects trading or scheduling.
Relevant notices are forwarded to the team with a summary or question.
The team discusses the impact, sometimes in a meeting, and asks follow-up questions of the ISO.
Comments on drafts are sent back by the stated deadline, and system changes are tested.
synthesis.approach: Route ISO and FERC notices into a single feed tagged by topic (price caps, settlements, operating procedures, outages, calls), and produce a short daily digest that flags notices touching active positions or systems, with a standard impact note format for the desk lead to complete.
synthesis.rationale: The work is triage of a high volume of notices, many routine. A checklist for assessing a notice's impact (pricing, scheduling, settlements, systems, comment deadline) makes the review consistent while the digest cuts the sorting; the judgement on market impact stays with people.
